answers.q1: Cargo (Rust). Install the Rust toolchain via rustup (rust-version 1.96 per Cargo.toml; CI pins 1.96.0), then run `cargo fetch` from the repo root to download dependencies. `cargo build --workspace` also fetches them.
answers.q2: `cargo test --workspace`. CI also runs `cargo test --verbose --workspace --features unstable-index` and `cargo test --verbose --workspace --features pcre2`, so those are the feature variants to check.
answers.q3: `cargo test --test integration regression::`. The integration test target is named `integration` (tests/tests.rs), and it pulls in tests/regression.rs as `mod regression;`, so the file is not a standalone target.
answers.q4: `cargo fmt --all --check` (the rustfmt job) and `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace` (the docs job). CI runs no clippy step.
answers.q5: Cargo.lock and fuzz/Cargo.lock are generated by Cargo (their header says so), so change them only through cargo commands. The man page, shell completions and deployment/ output are produced by the build or release process and are gitignored, not hand-edited. The zsh completion file crates/core/flags/complete/zsh.rs is maintained by hand. No vendored directories were found.

q1.reason: Identifies Cargo and gives `cargo fetch` / `cargo build --workspace`, matching accepted commands.

q2.reason: Gives `cargo test --workspace`, which matches the accept criterion; the extra feature variants are harmless.

q3.reason: `cargo test --test integration regression::` exactly matches an accepted command.

q4.reason: Gives `cargo fmt --all --check` plus the cargo doc command, and correctly states CI runs no clippy.

q5.reason: Names Cargo.lock as generated, which is accepted, but also claims the man page, completions and deployment/ output are generated build artifacts, which goes beyond the truth that nothing needs to be left unedited.
